newsitem.title: USA: Ohio muni bond tax case heads to U.S. high court.
newsitem.headline: Ohio muni bond tax case heads to U.S. high court.

text.p: A challenge to Ohio's tax on the income of out-of-state municipal bonds is heading back to the U.S. Supreme Court, an attorney representing the plaintiff in the case said Tuesday.
Sarah Weisenthal said a petition asking the high court to hear the case will be filed by the end of the month.
It will be the second time the supreme court will be asked to take up the question of whether or not Ohio's tax on out-of-state municipals is an unreasonable burden on interstate commerce.
In October 1995, the nation's high court declined to hear the first part of the case which sought a declaratory judgment that Ohio's in-state tax exemption was unconstitutional.
That action followed the Ohio Supreme Court's refusal to hear the case, and rulings by Ohio trial and appeals courts upholding the state's practice.

Lawyers for Serene Shaper, a Cleveland-area bondholder, then pursued the second part of the case seeking a refund of $6,000 in income taxes Shaper paid between 1988 and 1991 on interest earned from her out-of-state municipal bonds. That refund had been rejected by the Ohio revenue department and by the state tax appeals board.
Shaper's lawyers will now ask the U.S. Supreme Court to take up the refund question, after the Ohio Supreme Court in August upheld the tax appeals board's denial of a refund.
Clint Krislov, one of Shaper's attorneys, has said that the granting of the refund by a court would have to address the constitutionality of Ohio's tax practice.
